task: Check Java domain-handler acceptance against the C++ compiler using a bounded sample of standalone semantic fixtures.
observation: A check-only scan of the first 50 sorted top-level tests found Java accepted a value-returning handler that replies only in one branch and falls through otherwise. The C++ checker rejects the same modern minimal reproducer with `reply handler 'Worker.Maybe' must reply on every normal control-flow path`. Java had no main handler-body fallthrough check; adding it initially also rejected source-free imported handlers whose bodies are unavailable, so the check now skips source-free domains.
impact: The exercised Java-only acceptance is closed. The scan exposed six additional mismatches, grouped as one branch-confined open-vector inference case and five untyped handler payload/domain-specialization cases; these remain open. The bounded screen does not establish broad semantic parity.

resolution.summary: Java now rejects the reproduced missing-reply path and preserves source-free handler import tests; six other sample mismatches are still open.
